title: A setup is a job for every piece
outcomes: Gives the job of each move in one simple White setup (centre, development, castling)
Plays the next job of the setup in model positions
Prefers a clear developing move to holding an offered pawn when the two are about equal (a rule of thumb)
Sees that the setup stops mattering once a threat or a tactic appears

steps.text: A **setup** gives every piece a job: a pawn in the centre, knights and bishops out toward it, the king castled, the rooks joined. It is not a list of moves, because your opponent will not follow your list. The order can change; the reason for each move does not. Here is one White setup with the job of each move. Then you play the next job yourself.

steps.caption: One White setup, move by move. Watch the reason for each move, not the order.

line.say: Centre pawn. The f1 bishop goes from no moves to five.
Knight toward the centre. It attacks e5 and clears g1 for castling.
Bishop out. It aims at f7 and leaves f1 free for the rook.
Pawn support for e4. The c1 bishop gets a diagonal.

claims.statement: Before e4 the f1 bishop has no legal move.
After e4 the f1 bishop has five legal moves.
After Nf3 (and ...e5) the knight attacks e5.
After Bc4 the bishop attacks f7.
After d3 the e4 pawn is defended by a pawn.
After d3 the c1 bishop has five legal moves.

steps.text: A setup is a default, not a law. **Rule of thumb for club play:** when a pawn is offered and a developing move is about as good, develop. Extra pawns cost moves to keep. Some offered pawns are safe to take, so this is advice about your risk, not a ban. A setup also waits when the opponent has just made a threat: check that first.

steps.title: Grab the pawn, or follow the setup?
steps.prompt: The same question in two positions: is taking the offered pawn a mistake? Predict, then check.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** Each item can show three hints; a silent item turns hints and the engine off. Explanations quote engine scores in centipawns: 100 is about one pawn. The Openings page shows what players play; it gives no advice. The My plan page can hold an experiment: a baseline, practice and a later check. Next: four silent items.
